Kara no Kyoukai is a series of 7 movies adapted from Nasu's light novel of the same name. Chronologically, the events in the movies order them at 4, 1, 3, 2, 5, 6, 7, Epilogue. (Note that we will be watching them in release order.) Due to the intricacies of this order, there will be 2 threads: One for people watching it for the first time, and another for rewatches. This is because of 2 things:

  • It's too easy to just 'sneak a peek' at a spoiler, even when it's tagged.
  • Walls of spoiler text hurt the eyes
  • Chronological order of events and then the outcome of the final movie are complicated and interwoven
  • Rewatchers get absolute ability to discuss without fear
  • Fresh watchers get ability to enjoy it for the first time without fear

The first 4 movies are essentially set-up, the first movie especially throws you directly into the situation without context. Do not give up on the series, stick through until at least movie 5.

This map purportedly was made by the Bureau of Land Management, showing bigfoot sightings in Oregon. My thoughts in the comments.

So what do we have. A map of part of Oregon. With little symbols on it showing outlines of bigfoot-style footprints, as well as little Patty-shaped silhouettes. Being a lifelong Oregon resident, I'm familiar with a fair number of the areas shown on the map. A lot of these are in Southern and Eastern Oregon, in lots of scrubland and rocky landscapes. Is it interesting? Sure it is! Some of these areas are known to have a few bigfoot sightings to their credit. The idea that the BLM keeps a map of historical bigfoot sightings is pretty cool! However, what makes the question this video so so so much is all the other stuff about it.

First, it looks like it was just printed off a plotter-type printer, which are pretty easy to get access to. Especially with the big, dumb "you are not alone" slogan across the top. That would not fly in a government agency. Second, all the little bits of commentary printed on the map in other locations. These commentary bits make it remarkably obvious that this map, even if the original digital file is worth taking seriously, has already been edited by the filmmaker in some way or another. In fact, it would be very easy ta fabricate this whole thing. You upload a completely unrelated map into photoshop, make a couple stamps, go to town, add dates and a legend, then you're done!

Also the "rubber stamp" looking thing that says you shouldn't question the validity of the map, for some reason, makes me really really question the validity of the map.
